title: The axiom of choice: choice functions, well-ordering, and Zorn’s lemma
summary: Three equivalent existence principles, with an application to extending partial orders.
abstract: Selecting one element from each of many nonempty sets is easy when a common rule is available. The axiom of choice asserts that such a selection exists for every family, even without a given rule. The same assumption guarantees that every set can be arranged so each nonempty subset has a first element. It also guarantees a maximal object, one with no strictly larger object, in any nonempty partially ordered collection where every chain of comparable objects has an upper bound. This latter form, Zorn’s lemma, lets us extend any partial order to a total order that preserves its original comparisons.
